publish.title: What is a cookie, really?
publish.description: A short explainer of web cookies: what they are, how a login uses one, and how to control them.

scenes.headline: What is a cookie?
scenes.narration: Every site you visit can leave a small note in your browser. That note is called a cookie.

scenes.headline: Cookies in one line
scenes.narration: A cookie is a small piece of text. The site sets it, your browser stores it, and sends it back on every later request to that site.

definition.meaning: A small piece of data a site asks your browser to store and send back on later visits.

scenes.headline: How a login stays alive
scenes.narration: When you sign in, the site gives your browser a session cookie. Each new page request carries it, so the site can tell it is still you.
items: The site sets a session cookie
Your browser sends it back each time
The site knows it is you

scenes.headline: First party and third party
scenes.narration: A first-party cookie comes from the site you are visiting. A third-party cookie comes from a different site embedded in the page, and some of them are used to track you across sites.

left.label: First party
left.text: Set by the site you are on

right.label: Third party
right.text: Set by another site, some used to track you

scenes.headline: You are in control
scenes.narration: You can see, block and delete cookies in your browser settings. Blocking all of them breaks most logins, so many people block only the third-party kind.

scenes.headline: Look at your own cookies
scenes.narration: Open your browser's settings and see what is stored. You might be surprised.
